{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KKv6pX8KB5qAn9ty4TyB8o","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# MDFlow EHR, LLC DBA: MDFlow Systems — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-14\n     4→Developer website: https://www.mdflow.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→MDFlow Systems is a small, privately held healthcare IT company based in Miami, Florida (7715 NW 48th Street, Miami, FL 33166), incorporated in 2014 as MDFlow EHR, LLC. The company describes itself as having \"over a decade of experience\" providing healthcare software and services. MDFlow's primary market is **value-based care provider groups** — particularly staff-model medical groups operating under capitation contracts and sharing risk with health plans in South Florida. Their largest referenced customer, Community Medical Group, operates 18 medical centers with over 70,000 patients using MDFlow.\n     9→\n    10→The company offers three distinct product lines: (1) the MDFlow EHR and Patient Care Workflow Management System (the ONC-certified product), (2) the MDFlow Care Management System (a separate population health/case management platform), and (3) the MDFlow Hospitalist Management System (HMS). The company also offers a telemedicine platform, a mobile app, a non-emergency transportation management system (MDTrans), and HIT consulting services. MDFlow holds HITRUST CSF certification (achieved August 2022). The company's clients include managed care organizations and health plans such as Freedom Health, Optimum Healthcare, Solis Health Plans, and Cano Health, in addition to provider groups.\n    11→\n    12→MDFlow is not listed on G2, Capterra, or KLAS, suggesting a very small market footprint — likely focused on a niche of South Florida managed care/capitated provider groups.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: MDFlow EHR and Patient Care Workflow Management System\n    15→\n    16→CHPL ID: 11459 (15.11.09.3190.MDEP.08.00.1.240402)\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→The MDFlow EHR is a web-based (cloud/SaaS), ONC-certified electronic health records and patient care workflow management system. It was certified for version 8.0 on April 2, 2024. The product is internet-based, accessible from any computer via secured connection, and positions itself as enabling practices to \"go paperless.\" It is specifically designed for value-based care provider groups, with unique features for staff-model medical groups under capitation contracts.\n    21→\n    22→The certified module appears to be the EHR system itself. The Care Management System and Hospitalist Management System are separate products (the Care Management System is explicitly described as a distinct product line). However, the telemedicine platform is described as \"fully integrated into MDFlow EHR and Care Management System.\"\n    23→\n    24→### Users & Market\n    25→\n    26→**Target users**: Healthcare providers and supporting clinicians (per SED description), physicians, nurses, and clinical staff in ambulatory/primary care settings.\n    27→\n    28→**Clinical settings**: Primarily ambulatory/outpatient. The product targets staff-model medical groups, multi-site practice groups, and value-based care organizations operating under capitation and risk-sharing contracts. The South Florida managed care market appears to be their primary geography.\n    29→\n    30→**Known customers** (from testimonials and news):\n    31→- **Community Medical Group** — 18 medical centers, 70,000+ patients (largest referenced customer)\n    32→- **Plaza Medical Centers** — referenced in testimonials\n    33→- **Health Excel Inc.** — referenced in testimonials\n    34→- **Simply Healthcare Plans** — referenced in testimonials\n    35→- **Cano Health** — integrated MDFlow into their Population Health Management platform (April 2018 news)\n    36→\n    37→**Market size**: Very small vendor. No presence on major review platforms (G2, Capterra, KLAS). The company appears to serve a niche of South Florida managed care provider groups. The phone number is a direct Miami line (305-648-0028).\n    38→\n    39→### Modules & Functionality\n    40→\n    41→Based on the vendor's mandatory disclosures page, product documentation (DocPlayer archived materials), and the certified criteria list, the EHR includes:\n    42→\n    43→**Clinical Documentation & Charting**\n    44→- Electronic capture of patient demographics and medical records\n    45→- Clinical decision support (certified: (a)(2))\n    46→- Computerized Physician Order Entry (CPOE) for medications (certified: (a)(1))\n    47→- Implicit support for clinical notes/encounter documentation (core EHR function)\n    48→\n    49→**Medication Management**\n    50→- Electronic prescribing (e-prescribing) with drug interaction checking\n    51→- Medication reconciliation\n    52→- Formulary compliance checking\n    53→- PBM (Pharmaceutical Benefits Management) history — access to patient's previously filled medications from all prescribing physicians (via Surescripts/similar)\n    54→- Drug-drug, drug-allergy interaction checking (certified: (a)(5))\n    55→\n    56→**Lab & Diagnostic Integration**\n    57→- Automatic retrieval of patient lab test results and incorporation into the patient chart\n    58→- Immunization registry submission (certified: (h)(1))\n    59→\n    60→**Scheduling & Patient Flow**\n    61→- Appointment scheduling with transportation management\n    62→- Mobile app for viewing appointment schedules (iOS/Android, launched August 2017)\n    63→\n    64→**Health Information Exchange**\n    65→- Secure health information exchange in HL7, CCD, CCR, CCDA formats\n    66→- Transitions of care (certified: (b)(1))\n    67→- Direct secure messaging\n    68→- FHIR API access (certified: (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10))\n    69→\n    70→**Patient Engagement**\n    71→- Patient portal (mentioned on mandatory disclosures page)\n    72→- Telemedicine consultations (platform fully integrated with EHR since March 2016; sessions recorded and stored in patient's medical record)\n    73→- Secure messaging\n    74→\n    75→**Quality Measurement & Risk Adjustment**\n    76→- HCC/MRA (Hierarchical Condition Category / Medicare Risk Adjustment) scoring and management\n    77→- HCC disease group management\n    78→- Star Ratings tracking\n    79→- HEDIS measures\n    80→- Clinical quality measurement (PQRS & MIPS)\n    81→- Medical chart review functionality for risk adjustment\n    82→\n    83→**Reporting & Analytics**\n    84→- Data analytics and reporting tools that \"turn data into decisions\"\n    85→- Business intelligence reporting\n    86→- Quality measurement tracking\n    87→\n    88→**Document Management**\n    89→- Document management capabilities (referenced in the DocPlayer materials)\n    90→\n    91→**Mobile Access**\n    92→- MDFlow Mobile App (iOS and Android) — secure access to patient medical records and appointment schedules from smartphones and tablets\n    93→\n    94→### Data & Content\n    95→\n    96→Based on the features described above, the EHR stores or manages:\n    97→\n    98→- **Patient demographics** — explicitly mentioned as a core feature\n    99→- **Clinical encounter data / medical records** — core EHR function, explicitly mentioned\n   100→- **Medication data** — e-prescribing, medication reconciliation, PBM history, and drug interaction checking all imply medication lists, prescription records, and pharmacy data\n   101→- **Lab results** — automatically retrieved and incorporated into patient charts\n   102→- **Immunization records** — immunization registry submission (h)(1) certification\n   103→- **Appointment/scheduling data** — scheduling is a described feature with mobile access\n   104→- **Telemedicine session records** — the vendor explicitly states that telemedicine session information is \"recorded and stored in the patient's medical record\"\n   105→- **Quality/risk adjustment data** — HCC scores, Star Ratings, HEDIS, MIPS/PQRS metrics\n   106→- **Health information exchange documents** — CCD, CCR, CCDA, HL7 messages\n   107→- **Secure messages** — secure messaging is a listed feature\n   108→- **Documents** — document management is referenced\n   109→\n   110→**Unclear / Not mentioned:**\n   111→- **Billing and claims data**: The mandatory disclosures page mentions pricing based on practice size and the product promises \"revenue enhancement,\" but the EHR product page does not explicitly describe billing, claims submission, or revenue cycle management as features. The Hospitalist Management System (a separate product) explicitly includes billing and revenue cycle management. It is unclear whether the EHR has built-in billing or whether billing is handled externally or through a separate module.\n   112→- **Clinical notes structure**: While encounter documentation is implied, the specific note templates, structured data elements, and clinical note types are not described in available materials.\n   113→- **Problem lists / diagnosis data**: While HCC management implies diagnosis coding, explicit problem list functionality is not described on available pages.\n   114→- **Allergy data**: Drug-allergy interaction checking (a)(5) certification implies allergy data is stored, but it's not explicitly described as a feature.\n   115→- **Vital signs**: Not explicitly mentioned in available materials, though standard for an EHR.\n   116→- **Imaging/radiology**: Not mentioned anywhere in the EHR product materials.\n   117→- **Referral management**: Not mentioned.\n   118→- **Orders beyond medications**: CPOE is listed for medications; unclear if lab orders, imaging orders, or referral orders are managed.\n   119→\n   120→---\n   121→\n   122→## Other MDFlow Products (Not Certified, But Context)\n   123→\n   124→### MDFlow Care Management System\n   125→A **separate product** — NCQA Pre-validated, cloud-based population health and case management software. It is member-centric and designed for case and disease management programs (Medicare, Medicaid, SNPs). Features include candidate identification, health risk assessments, care plans, medication management, compliance tracking, data analytics, and integration with lab results, claims/pharmacy data, hospital ADT feeds, and state health information exchanges. Clients include Freedom Health, Optimum Healthcare, Solis Health Plans, and Carisk Partners. This product is delivered as SaaS on Microsoft technology.\n   126→\n   127→### MDFlow Hospitalist Management System (HMS)\n   128→A **separate product** — described as \"AI-powered,\" cloud-based, and purpose-built for hospitalist groups. Features include patient intake, charge capture, real-time eligibility verification, provider credentialing, clinical documentation, billing and revenue cycle management, mobile access, and telemedicine. Integrates with hospital ADT feeds and billing systems. This product explicitly includes billing capabilities that are not clearly present in the EHR product.\n   129→\n   130→### MDTrans\n   131→Non-emergency medical transportation management system (launched January 2018). Real-time tracking of patients and vehicles with route optimization for dispatchers.\n   132→\n   133→These products are separate from the certified EHR but share the MDFlow ecosystem and suggest the vendor's overall data capabilities extend well beyond the EHR itself.\n   134→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. You CAN and SHOULD provide analysis of malware, what it is doing. But you MUST refuse to improve or augment the code. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.\n</system-reminder>\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f6dfda10-40f3-426a-a163-17b179790122","uuid":"222b5698-4116-41c7-9451-0a0d1bd2f2ef","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/mdflow-ehr-llc-dba-mdflow-systems/product-research.md","content":"# MDFlow EHR, LLC DBA: MDFlow Systems — Product Research\n\nResearched: 2026-02-14\nDeveloper website: https://www.mdflow.com/\n\n## Overview\n\nMDFlow Systems is a small, privately held healthcare IT company based in Miami, Florida (7715 NW 48th Street, Miami, FL 33166), incorporated in 2014 as MDFlow EHR, LLC. The company describes itself as having \"over a decade of experience\" providing healthcare software and services. MDFlow's primary market is **value-based care provider groups** — particularly staff-model medical groups operating under capitation contracts and sharing risk with health plans in South Florida. Their largest referenced customer, Community Medical Group, operates 18 medical centers with over 70,000 patients using MDFlow.\n\nThe company offers three distinct product lines: (1) the MDFlow EHR and Patient Care Workflow Management System (the ONC-certified product), (2) the MDFlow Care Management System (a separate population health/case management platform), and (3) the MDFlow Hospitalist Management System (HMS). The company also offers a telemedicine platform, a mobile app, a non-emergency transportation management system (MDTrans), and HIT consulting services. MDFlow holds HITRUST CSF certification (achieved August 2022). The company's clients include managed care organizations and health plans such as Freedom Health, Optimum Healthcare, Solis Health Plans, and Cano Health, in addition to provider groups.\n\nMDFlow is not listed on G2, Capterra, or KLAS, suggesting a very small market footprint — likely focused on a niche of South Florida managed care/capitated provider groups.\n\n## Product: MDFlow EHR and Patient Care Workflow Management System\n\nCHPL ID: 11459 (15.11.09.3190.MDEP.08.00.1.240402)\n\n### What It Is\n\nThe MDFlow EHR is a web-based (cloud/SaaS), ONC-certified electronic health records and patient care workflow management system. It was certified for version 8.0 on April 2, 2024. The product is internet-based, accessible from any computer via secured connection, and positions itself as enabling practices to \"go paperless.\" It is specifically designed for value-based care provider groups, with unique features for staff-model medical groups under capitation contracts.\n\nThe certified module appears to be the EHR system itself. The Care Management System and Hospitalist Management System are separate products (the Care Management System is explicitly described as a distinct product line). However, the telemedicine platform is described as \"fully integrated into MDFlow EHR and Care Management System.\"\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**Target users**: Healthcare providers and supporting clinicians (per SED description), physicians, nurses, and clinical staff in ambulatory/primary care settings.\n\n**Clinical settings**: Primarily ambulatory/outpatient. The product targets staff-model medical groups, multi-site practice groups, and value-based care organizations operating under capitation and risk-sharing contracts. The South Florida managed care market appears to be their primary geography.\n\n**Known customers** (from testimonials and news):\n- **Community Medical Group** — 18 medical centers, 70,000+ patients (largest referenced customer)\n- **Plaza Medical Centers** — referenced in testimonials\n- **Health Excel Inc.** — referenced in testimonials\n- **Simply Healthcare Plans** — referenced in testimonials\n- **Cano Health** — integrated MDFlow into their Population Health Management platform (April 2018 news)\n\n**Market size**: Very small vendor. No presence on major review platforms (G2, Capterra, KLAS). The company appears to serve a niche of South Florida managed care provider groups. The phone number is a direct Miami line (305-648-0028).\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on the vendor's mandatory disclosures page, product documentation (DocPlayer archived materials), and the certified criteria list, the EHR includes:\n\n**Clinical Documentation & Charting**\n- Electronic capture of patient demographics and medical records\n- Clinical decision support (certified: (a)(2))\n- Computerized Physician Order Entry (CPOE) for medications (certified: (a)(1))\n- Implicit support for clinical notes/encounter documentation (core EHR function)\n\n**Medication Management**\n- Electronic prescribing (e-prescribing) with drug interaction checking\n- Medication reconciliation\n- Formulary compliance checking\n- PBM (Pharmaceutical Benefits Management) history — access to patient's previously filled medications from all prescribing physicians (via Surescripts/similar)\n- Drug-drug, drug-allergy interaction checking (certified: (a)(5))\n\n**Lab & Diagnostic Integration**\n- Automatic retrieval of patient lab test results and incorporation into the patient chart\n- Immunization registry submission (certified: (h)(1))\n\n**Scheduling & Patient Flow**\n- Appointment scheduling with transportation management\n- Mobile app for viewing appointment schedules (iOS/Android, launched August 2017)\n\n**Health Information Exchange**\n- Secure health information exchange in HL7, CCD, CCR, CCDA formats\n- Transitions of care (certified: (b)(1))\n- Direct secure messaging\n- FHIR API access (certified: (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10))\n\n**Patient Engagement**\n- Patient portal (mentioned on mandatory disclosures page)\n- Telemedicine consultations (platform fully integrated with EHR since March 2016; sessions recorded and stored in patient's medical record)\n- Secure messaging\n\n**Quality Measurement & Risk Adjustment**\n- HCC/MRA (Hierarchical Condition Category / Medicare Risk Adjustment) scoring and management\n- HCC disease group management\n- Star Ratings tracking\n- HEDIS measures\n- Clinical quality measurement (PQRS & MIPS)\n- Medical chart review functionality for risk adjustment\n\n**Reporting & Analytics**\n- Data analytics and reporting tools that \"turn data into decisions\"\n- Business intelligence reporting\n- Quality measurement tracking\n\n**Document Management**\n- Document management capabilities (referenced in the DocPlayer materials)\n\n**Mobile Access**\n- MDFlow Mobile App (iOS and Android) — secure access to patient medical records and appointment schedules from smartphones and tablets\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the features described above, the EHR stores or manages:\n\n- **Patient demographics** — explicitly mentioned as a core feature\n- **Clinical encounter data / medical records** — core EHR function, explicitly mentioned\n- **Medication data** — e-prescribing, medication reconciliation, PBM history, and drug interaction checking all imply medication lists, prescription records, and pharmacy data\n- **Lab results** — automatically retrieved and incorporated into patient charts\n- **Immunization records** — immunization registry submission (h)(1) certification\n- **Appointment/scheduling data** — scheduling is a described feature with mobile access\n- **Telemedicine session records** — the vendor explicitly states that telemedicine session information is \"recorded and stored in the patient's medical record\"\n- **Quality/risk adjustment data** — HCC scores, Star Ratings, HEDIS, MIPS/PQRS metrics\n- **Health information exchange documents** — CCD, CCR, CCDA, HL7 messages\n- **Secure messages** — secure messaging is a listed feature\n- **Documents** — document management is referenced\n\n**Unclear / Not mentioned:**\n- **Billing and claims data**: The mandatory disclosures page mentions pricing based on practice size and the product promises \"revenue enhancement,\" but the EHR product page does not explicitly describe billing, claims submission, or revenue cycle management as features. The Hospitalist Management System (a separate product) explicitly includes billing and revenue cycle management. It is unclear whether the EHR has built-in billing or whether billing is handled externally or through a separate module.\n- **Clinical notes structure**: While encounter documentation is implied, the specific note templates, structured data elements, and clinical note types are not described in available materials.\n- **Problem lists / diagnosis data**: While HCC management implies diagnosis coding, explicit problem list functionality is not described on available pages.\n- **Allergy data**: Drug-allergy interaction checking (a)(5) certification implies allergy data is stored, but it's not explicitly described as a feature.\n- **Vital signs**: Not explicitly mentioned in available materials, though standard for an EHR.\n- **Imaging/radiology**: Not mentioned anywhere in the EHR product materials.\n- **Referral management**: Not mentioned.\n- **Orders beyond medications**: CPOE is listed for medications; unclear if lab orders, imaging orders, or referral orders are managed.\n\n---\n\n## Other MDFlow Products (Not Certified, But Context)\n\n### MDFlow Care Management System\nA **separate product** — NCQA Pre-validated, cloud-based population health and case management software. It is member-centric and designed for case and disease management programs (Medicare, Medicaid, SNPs). Features include candidate identification, health risk assessments, care plans, medication management, compliance tracking, data analytics, and integration with lab results, claims/pharmacy data, hospital ADT feeds, and state health information exchanges. Clients include Freedom Health, Optimum Healthcare, Solis Health Plans, and Carisk Partners. This product is delivered as SaaS on Microsoft technology.\n\n### MDFlow Hospitalist Management System (HMS)\nA **separate product** — described as \"AI-powered,\" cloud-based, and purpose-built for hospitalist groups. Integrates with hospital ADT feeds and billing systems. This product explicitly includes billing capabilities that are not clearly present in the EHR product.\n\n### MDTrans\nNon-emergency medical transportation management system (launched January 2018). Real-time tracking of patients and vehicles with route optimization for dispatchers.\n\nThese products are separate from the certified EHR but share the MDFlow ecosystem and suggest the vendor's overall data capabilities extend well beyond the EHR itself.\n","numLines":134,"startLine":1,"totalLines":134}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015gu593PMZPuei4TKgnUq9J","type":"tool_result","content":"170.315(b) (10) Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export in MDFlow™ EHR V 8.0\n\nThe patient Electronic Health Information (EHI) export contains data stored in the patient's chart in\nthe SQL database. The C-CDA or Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture or CSV Text file or\nPDF File is used for health information exchange.\n\n\nWe support multiple file formats for export patient EHI data.\n\n\n\nThe primary patient’s EHI export format is CCDA.\n\n\n\nOur system can also accommodate our clients’ special and customized requests of the EHI\nexport. The proprietary file format CSV Text file and/or PDF File are used in these cases.\n\n\n\nOur system can export single patient’s EHI or a group of patients’ EHI.\n\n\n\nThe Zip file is used to compress the data if the file size is large.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f6dfda10-40f3-426a-a163-17b179790122","uuid":"afdd2614-2214-4ab2-9742-aa19bb4fa714","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"170.315(b) (10) Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export in MDFlow™ EHR V 8.0\n\nThe patient Electronic Health Information (EHI) export contains data stored in the patient's chart in\nthe SQL database. 8.0\nINTRODUCTION\n\nIn this documentation we will list all the steps required to access protected health information based on the documentation of an open API. The\nAPI makes health information broadly available using FHIR®, a set of clinical interoperability resources under the umbrella of the HL7 standards\norganization. FHIR is based on common web standards can be reached through a RESTful protocol in which each FHIR resource has a known\nURL. This document describes OAuth 2.0 for client applications to authorize, authenticate, and integrate with FHIR-based data systems.\nWe follow Smart-On-FHIR authentication (OAuth2) and authorization (Ref. http://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/toc.html )\n\nFHIR Endpoints\nNote: Production and Test Server endpoints are subject to change.\n\nProduction Endpoint\n•\n•\n\nFHIR : https://fhir.mdflow.com:8443/fhirserver/fhir/\nAuthentication Server: https://oauth.mdflow.com/\n\nTest Server Endpoint\n•\n•\n\nFHIR : https://fhir.mdflow.com:8443/fhirserver/fhir/\nAuthentication Server: https://oauth.mdflow.com/\n\nTypes of Smart-On-FHIR applications\n•\n\nStandalone App : SMART on FHIR confidential client with a patient context, refresh token, and OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity\ntoken.\n\n•\n\nEHR Embedded app: Demonstrate the ability to perform an EHR launch to a SMART on FHIR\n\n•\n\nSmart Backend Services App (Multi-patient authorization and API) : These are server-to-server backend applications e.g. Export\nclinical data for multiple patients in a group. This app is system level app without any UI.\n\nTypes of Authentications supported\n•\n\nSymmetric (“client secret”) authentication (HL7.FHIR.UV.SMART-APP-LAUNCH\\Example App Launch for Symmetric Client Auth - FHIR\nv4.0.1)\n\n•\n\nAsymmetric (“private key JWT”) authentication (HL7.FHIR.UV.SMART-APP-LAUNCH\\Example App Launch for Asymmetric Client Auth\n- FHIR v4.0.1)\n\n•\n\nPublic Clients (HL7.FHIR.UV.SMART-APP-LAUNCH\\Example App Launch for Public Client - FHIR v4.0.1)\n\nSteps for Smart App Launch\n1.\n\nClient App Registration\n\n2.\n\nRetrieve .well-known/smart-configuration\n\n3.\n\nObtain authorization code\n\n4.\n\nObtain access token\n\n5.\n\nAccess FHIR API\n\n6.\n\nRefresh Token to obtain new access token\n\n\fClient APP Registration\nBefore a SMART app can run against an EHR, the app must be registered with that EHR’s authorization service. We are using OAuth 2.0 Client\nRegistration.\n\nClient App Request process\n•\n\nThird-party application must sign the API Subscription Agreement with following details\no\no\no\no\no\n\n•\n\nThe app name\nThe necessary APIs / Scopes\nAny redirect URIs\nLaunch URL (optional)\nURL to JWK Set (Only for apps supporting asymmetric client authentication).\n\nThe application is created by the EHR admin after confirming the app’s registration parameters and communicates a client_id to the\napp.\no FHIR APIs (of any supported version) listed within the USCDI v1 core data set will be supported\no Only reads data from FHIR server\n\nRetrieve .well-known/smart-configuration\nIn order to obtain launch context and request authorization to access FHIR resources, the app discovers the EHR FHIR server’s SMART\nconfiguration metadata, including OAuth authorization_endpoint and token_endpoint URLs.\nFHIR server makes SMART configuration available from well-known endpoint. You can get Authorization end point and token endpoint.\n\nRequest\nGET 200 https://yourfhirserver.com/r4/.well-known/smart-configuration\n\nResponse\n{\n\"capabilities\": [\n\"launch-ehr\",\n\"launch-standalone\",\n\"client-public\",\n\"client-confidential-symmetric\",\n\"sso-openid-connect\",\n\"context-banner\",\n\"context-style\",\n\"context-ehr-patient\",\n\"context-ehr-encounter\",\n\"context-standalone-patient\",\n\"context-standalone-encounter\",\n\"permission-offline\",\n\"permission-patient\",\n\"permission-user\"\n],\n\"revocation_endpoint\": \"https://oauth.mdflow.com/oauth/token/revoke-token\",\n\"authorization_endpoint\": \"https://oauth.mdflow.com/oauth/authorization\",\n\"token_endpoint\": \"https://oauth.mdflow.com/oauth/token\"\n}\n\nError codes\nJSON response is returned from the FHIR Server along with the code\n200: Ok\n401: Unauthorized\n400: Bad Request\n500: Internal Server Error\n\n\fObtain authorization code\nThe app supplies the following parameters to the EHR’s “authorize” endpoint.\n\nParameters\n\nresponse_type\n\nrequired\n\nFixed value: It is designed with the patient's care workflow in mind to help practices streamline and enhance the flow of information throughout the patient's medical care lifecycle. As the centralized electronic repository of medical data, all the medical information of the patient is accurately recorded and electronically stored in MDFlow system. MDFlow EHR System addresses the needs of pre-visit functionality, visit functionality and post-visit functionality for the small practices to large physician groups with multiple locations. Healthcare providers could access patient’s medical information from office, home, hospital, or from multiple offices using any computer via secured internet connection at anytime.\"\n  uid=1_18 LineBreak \"\n\"\n  uid=1_19 LineBreak \"\n\"\n  uid=1_20 StaticText \"MDFlow EHR System also offers a list of features specific designed for the staff-model medical groups who are under the capitation contracts and sharing the risk with the health plans.\"\n  uid=1_21 LineBreak \"\n\"\n  uid=1_22 LineBreak \"\n\"\n  uid=1_23 StaticText \"MDFlow offers a winning combination of cost reduction, operational efficiency and revenue enhancement, as well as increase patient’s safety and satisfaction. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01F9yGJfxJByMsrC6PQSzXnt","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01JxJEwXQqUodVJyf7weWo8G","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/mdflow-ehr-llc-dba-mdflow-systems/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# MDFlow EHR, LLC DBA: MDFlow Systems — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-14\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://www.mdflow.com/EHIExport.pdf\n- CHPL IDs: 11459\n- Product: MDFlow EHR and Patient Care Workflow Management System v8.0\n- Certification date: 2024-04-02\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\nThe registered URL is a direct PDF download:\n\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://www.mdflow.com/EHIExport.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n# HTTP/2 200, Content-Type: application/pdf, Content-Length: 442126\n```\n\nDownloaded the primary file:\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://www.mdflow.com/EHIExport.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o EHIExport.pdf\n```\n\nThen checked the mandatory disclosures page (https://www.mdflow.com/www/mdflow-electronics-health-records.html) for additional documentation. Found these EHI-relevant links in the compliance section near the bottom of the page:\n\n1. \"EHI Export Iinformation\" → https://www.mdflow.com/EHIExport.pdf (same as registered URL)\n2. \"EHI B10 Export\" → https://www.mdflow.com/www/pdf%20files/EHI%20B10-Export.pdf\n3. \"API Documentation (g7910)\" → https://www.mdflow.com/www/pdf%20files/API%20Documentation%20(g7910).pdf\n4. \"Json\" → https://www.mdflow.com/www/pdf%20files/ValidURLs.json\n\nDownloaded all three additional files:\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://www.mdflow.com/www/pdf%20files/EHI%20B10-Export.pdf\" -o EHI-B10-Export.pdf\ncurl -sL \"https://www.mdflow.com/www/pdf%20files/API%20Documentation%20(g7910).pdf\" -o API-Documentation-g7910.pdf\ncurl -sL \"https://www.mdflow.com/www/pdf%20files/ValidURLs.json\" -o ValidURLs.json\n```\n\nAlso captured a full-page screenshot of the mandatory disclosures page.\n\n## What Was Found\n\n### EHIExport.pdf (registered URL — 1 page, v8.0)\nA single-page PDF with the MDFlow logo and a brief description of the EHI export. The complete text states:\n- The export contains data stored in the patient's chart in the SQL database\n- Supported formats: C-CDA, CSV text file, or PDF\n- The **primary** export format is C-CDA\n- CSV and PDF are available for \"special and customized requests\"\n- Can export single patient or group of patients\n- ZIP compression is used for large files\n\nNo data dictionary, no field definitions, no schema, no sample data, no screenshots, no procedural instructions.\n\n### EHI B10-Export.pdf (1 page, v8.1)\nAn even more minimal document than the registered PDF. For version 8.1, it states:\n- The export contains data from the patient's chart\n- Multiple file formats are used\n- ZIP is used as the archive format\n- C-CDA is the health information exchange format\n- The export file is a ZIP containing ZIP files of C-CDAs\n- Each patient encounter has a C-CDA in the ZIP archive\n\nThis is marginally more specific — it clarifies the structure as a ZIP of per-encounter C-CDA ZIPs — but still provides no data dictionary or field-level documentation.\n\n### API Documentation (g7910).pdf (58 pages, v8.0)\nA comprehensive FHIR API document covering the SMART on FHIR authentication flow and individual FHIR resource endpoints. This is the (g)(7)/(g)(9)/(g)(10) documentation, **not** the (b)(10) EHI export. It covers:\n- SMART App Launch with OAuth 2.0 (standalone, EHR-embedded, backend services)\n- Symmetric and asymmetric authentication\n- Individual FHIR R4 resource endpoints: Patient, AllergyIntolerance, CarePlan, CareTeam, Condition, ImplantableDevice, DiagnosticReport/ClinicalNotes/DocumentReference, Observation (labs), Goal, Immunization, Medication, SmokingStatus, Procedure, Provenance, VitalSigns\n- Complete Patient Summary (CCDA) endpoint\n- Search for Patient, Encounter\n- Error handling\n\nThe FHIR resources listed are the standard US Core / USCDI v1 set. There is no mention of bulk data export being used for (b)(10), and this document is clearly the (g)(10) standardized API documentation.\n\n### ValidURLs.json\nA FHIR Bundle (type: collection) containing two Endpoint resources and two Organization resources. This lists the FHIR server endpoints (https://fhir.mdflow.com:8443/fhirserver/fhir/) for two test organizations. This is a (g)(10) Service Base URL artifact, not related to EHI export.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe EHI export documentation is profoundly vague — it says only that the export \"contains data stored in the patient's chart in the SQL database\" without specifying what data elements, tables, or clinical domains are included. The primary format is C-CDA per encounter, with CSV and PDF available \"for customized requests.\"\n\n**The critical question is what a C-CDA per encounter actually contains.** Standard C-CDA documents (CCD or Continuity of Care Document) typically include: demographics, problems, medications, allergies, immunizations, vital signs, procedures, lab results, and clinical notes for an encounter. This would cover core clinical data but leaves major gaps relative to the full designated record set.\n\nBased on the product research, MDFlow stores the following data domains. Assessment of likely export coverage:\n\n| Domain | Likely in C-CDA export? | Notes |\n|--------|------------------------|-------|\n| Patient demographics | Yes | Standard C-CDA section |\n| Problem lists / diagnoses | Yes | Standard C-CDA section |\n| Medications / e-prescribing | Yes | Standard C-CDA section |\n| Allergies | Yes | Standard C-CDA section |\n| Lab results | Yes | Standard C-CDA section |\n| Vital signs | Yes | Standard C-CDA section |\n| Immunizations | Yes | Standard C-CDA section |\n| Procedures | Yes | Standard C-CDA section |\n| Clinical notes / encounter documentation | Partially | C-CDA can include narrative sections |\n| HCC/MRA scores, Star Ratings, HEDIS | **Unclear** | Not standard C-CDA content |\n| Scheduling / appointments | **No** | Not part of C-CDA |\n| Telemedicine session records | **Unclear** | May be in notes, but session recordings likely not |\n| Billing / charges / claims | **No** | Not standard C-CDA content |\n| PBM history (pharmacy benefits) | **Unclear** | Medication history may partially cover this |\n| Referrals / utilization management | **Unclear** | May be in C-CDA referral sections |\n| Secure messages | **No** | Not part of C-CDA |\n| Scanned documents | **Unclear** | C-CDA can embed documents, but unclear if MDFlow includes them |\n| Quality measures (PQRS/MIPS) | **No** | Not standard C-CDA content |\n\nThe documentation mentions CSV and PDF as alternative formats for \"customized requests,\" which suggests the vendor may provide broader exports on request, but there is no documentation of what those CSV or PDF exports contain, what fields are included, or how to request them.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses **C-CDA** (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture) as its primary format, packaged as a ZIP file containing per-encounter C-CDA ZIP archives. C-CDA is a well-established HL7 standard, which is good for interoperability — but it is a **clinical summary** standard, not a comprehensive database export format.\n\nC-CDA was designed for transitions of care, not for complete EHI export. It has well-defined sections for core clinical data (the same data domains covered by USCDI/US Core) but does not naturally accommodate:\n- Billing and financial data\n- Administrative data (scheduling, referral tracking)\n- Risk adjustment and quality measurement data\n- Custom workflow data specific to value-based care operations\n\nThis creates a strong suspicion that MDFlow's (b)(10) export is functionally equivalent to their (g)(10) clinical data — just packaged as C-CDA documents rather than via FHIR API. The documentation does not describe any mechanism for exporting data that falls outside standard C-CDA sections.\n\nA third party receiving this export could reconstruct a clinical summary per encounter, but would likely miss billing records, quality scores, custom assessments, and operational data that MDFlow stores as part of the patient's designated record set.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation quality is **extremely poor** — among the worst possible for a certified product:\n\n- The registered EHI Export PDF is a single page with 5 bullet points and no technical substance\n- The supplemental B10-Export PDF is also a single page with even less content\n- There is **no data dictionary** — zero documentation of what specific data elements are exported\n- There are **no field definitions**, data types, constraints, or value sets\n- There are **no sample files or worked examples**\n- There are **no screenshots** of the export interface\n- There are **no procedural instructions** for performing an export\n- There is **no schema documentation** for the C-CDA templates used\n- A developer could not implement an import of this data based solely on this documentation — they would need to know C-CDA generically, then examine actual export files to understand MDFlow's specific implementation\n\nThe API Documentation PDF (58 pages) is by contrast quite detailed for the FHIR (g)(10) API, with full endpoint descriptions, request/response examples, and OAuth2 flow documentation. This disparity suggests the vendor invested real effort in the (g)(10) API but treated (b)(10) as a compliance checkbox.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Field-level documentation**: None. Not even table or section names.\n- **Coded fields / value sets**: Not documented.\n- **Relationships between entities**: Not documented. The per-encounter ZIP structure is described but nothing about how encounters relate to each other or to the patient.\n- **Versioning**: The original PDF references v8.0, the supplemental B10-Export.pdf references v8.1. No change history.\n\n### The (b)(10) vs (g)(10) Assessment\n\nWhile MDFlow's EHI export uses C-CDA rather than FHIR, the same conceptual problem applies: C-CDA, like FHIR US Core, covers the standard clinical summary data but not the full designated record set. MDFlow's product stores significant data beyond what C-CDA naturally represents — particularly HCC/MRA risk adjustment scores, quality measures, scheduling data, and value-based care workflow data that is central to the product's purpose.\n\nThe vendor mentions CSV and PDF as alternative export formats for \"customized requests,\" which could theoretically cover broader data domains, but these are undocumented. There is no data dictionary, no field list, no sample — nothing to indicate what a CSV export contains or how to interpret it.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.mdflow.com/EHIExport.pdf (no redirect)\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (for registered URL); one_click from mandatory disclosures page for supplemental files\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- No obstacles encountered. All URLs returned HTTP 200 with expected content types.\n- The MFA PDF (mfa.pdf) linked from the same disclosures page is about multi-factor authentication, not EHI export — skipped.\n- The link text on the disclosures page contains a typo (\"Iinformation\") and the MFA link text appears garbled (\"Multi-Factor Authentication IJson URLEHI Export Iinformation\"), suggesting sloppy HTML editing.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":391,"cache_read_input_tokens":58639,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":391},"output_tokens":25,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f6dfda10-40f3-426a-a163-17b179790122","uuid":"cbc674d8-3954-4459-ad0f-42ff066d1e2b"}
